spec: Build a customer loyalty-points service. Customer accounts live in DynamoDB. Purchases are submitted to a REST API with an idempotency key and queued on SQS for asynchronous point accrual; processing the same key twice must not double-award points. When a customer's balance crosses 1000 points an SNS notification announces their upgrade to gold tier. Every balance change is also appended to an audit log in S3. Include endpoints to check balances and list a customer's transactions.

complexity.rationale: Idempotent asynchronous accrual, tier notification, and audit logging span four services.

congruence_checklist: DynamoDB table for accounts and transactions
S3 audit log of balance changes
GET endpoint listing a customer's transactions

plan.summary: A FastAPI customer loyalty-points backend. Customers are stored in a DynamoDB table with their current point balance and tier. Purchases are submitted to a REST endpoint with a client-supplied idempotency key; the API records the key in a DynamoDB idempotency table (conditional write) and enqueues the purchase on SQS for asynchronous accrual. An SQS-triggered Lambda worker consumes purchase messages, atomically increments the customer's balance, writes an audit-log JSON object to S3 for every balance change, and publishes an SNS notification when a balance crosses 1000 points and the customer is upgraded to gold tier. The API also exposes balance lookup, transaction listing, and idempotent replay-safe purchase submission. Callers are internal e-commerce checkout services and customer-facing account dashboards.

endpoints.purpose: Create a customer loyalty account (id, email, name) in DynamoDB with zero balance and 'standard' tier.
Fetch a customer's profile record including tier and created timestamp.
Return the customer's current point balance and loyalty tier.
List the customer's purchase/accrual transactions from DynamoDB, newest first, with a limit/pagination cursor.

Submit a purchase with an Idempotency-Key; reserve the key in the idempotency table and enqueue the purchase on SQS for asynchronous point accrual. Returns 202 with the transaction id, or the previously stored result if the key was already seen.
Look up the processing status/result recorded for a given idempotency key.
List S3 audit-log entry keys (and optionally fetch entries) recorded for that customer's balance changes.
Liveness/readiness probe reporting reachability of DynamoDB, SQS, SNS and S3 dependencies.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-customers
aws_resources.justification: Stores customer accounts, point balances and tier; read by the balance endpoint and atomically updated by the accrual worker.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-transactions
aws_resources.justification: Stores per-customer purchase/accrual transactions (PK customer_id, SK transaction_id) backing the list-transactions endpoint.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-idempotency
aws_resources.justification: Conditional-write store of idempotency keys with TTL so submitting or processing the same purchase key twice never double-awards points.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-purchases-queue
aws_resources.justification: The purchases endpoint enqueues each accepted purchase here for asynchronous point accrual, decoupling the REST API from processing.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-purchases-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Redrive target for purchase messages that fail processing repeatedly, so poison messages do not block accrual.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-accrual-worker
aws_resources.justification: Cloud-side asynchronous consumer of the SQS purchase queue: applies the idempotency check, increments the balance, writes the S3 audit entry and publishes the SNS tier-upgrade event.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-tier-upgrades
aws_resources.justification: Publishes a gold-tier upgrade notification when a customer's balance crosses 1000 points.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-audit-log
aws_resources.justification: Append-only audit log: one JSON object per balance change, keyed by customer and timestamp; listed by the audit-log endpoint.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-accrual-worker-role
aws_resources.justification: Execution role for the accrual Lambda granting SQS receive/delete, DynamoDB read/update on the customer, transaction and idempotency tables, S3 PutObject, SNS Publish and CloudWatch Logs write.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-api-service-user
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege identity/policy used by the externally hosted FastAPI service for DynamoDB access, SQS SendMessage and S3 list/get on the audit bucket.

aws_resources.name: /aws/lambda/loyalty-accrual-worker
aws_resources.justification: Log group for the accrual worker plus an alarm on DLQ depth for operational visibility into failed accruals.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-api-config
aws_resources.justification: Holds the API key/shared secret used to authenticate purchase submissions from checkout clients; read by the FastAPI service at startup.

assumptions: Point accrual rule is not specified: assume 1 point per whole USD (amount_cents / 100, floored).

Tier thresholds beyond gold are not specified: assume two tiers, 'standard' below 1000 points and 'gold' at 1000 or more; the upgrade SNS notification fires only on the transition, not on every subsequent change.
The idempotency key is supplied via an 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header (also accepted in the body) and is unique per purchase submission; keys are retained for 30 days via DynamoDB TTL.
Duplicate purchase submissions return 200 with the stored/original result instead of re-enqueuing; first-time submissions return 202 Accepted.
Audit-log objects are written as JSON at key customers/{customer_id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{timestamp}-{transaction_id}.json with bucket versioning enabled for immutability.
Transactions are listed newest-first using a descending sort on a time-ordered transaction_id (ULID) with a limit of 50 and an opaque pagination cursor.
No end-user auth system is specified: assume a static API key from Secrets Manager for service-to-service calls; customer identity is passed explicitly in the request.
SNS has no concrete subscriber in the spec: the topic is created and published to, with subscription wiring left to operators.
Point redemption/spending is out of scope; only accrual is implemented.
The FastAPI service runs outside AWS (started by the harness) and reaches LocalStack endpoints via boto3; no API Gateway is provisioned since no cloud-side HTTP entry point is required.
